answer: The naive design trusts a signed claim forever. This one samples 2% of claims each epoch, re-runs them, and claws back three epochs of credit when a replay turns up, so a copied submission costs the attacker three epochs of income plus the audit fee. A 200-account farm meets the sample about four times per epoch. The kernel is the replay check, not the signature; an ember of history and an opal of reputation are both worth nothing after one replay.
